finding: Every props-v1 family's evaluation scores an absent-from-boxscore candidate as ACTUAL=0, while a candidate who appears with zero family opportunities is excluded (void). Prop markets void a DNP, so the two branches are inconsistent — and the absent branch is large: 48% of rush-yds points, 31% of receptions/receiving points, 42% of pass-yds points.

measurementLane_presentOnly.note: --present-only diagnose lane, 2025, identical code and baselines on identical points; treats EVERY absence as void — an OVERSHOOT (an active player with zero touches settles 0, not void), so this is the pessimistic bound, not the truth.

player_rush_yds.reading: LOSES to the share-volume baseline and fails calibration on the present-only bound

player_receptions.reading: still beats baselines but breaches the 0.88 coverage edge and the calibration bar on this bound

interpretation: The published families' bar-clearing evidence depends materially on the absent-as-zero branch. The market-matching population lies BETWEEN the two bounds: absent candidates split into inactive (void) and active-without-touches (settles 0), indistinguishable in the current corpus.
This is an evaluation-population question, not proof the models are bad — but it caps what the receipts may claim until resolved.
The anytime-TD family is unaffected: its own receipt evaluates under explicit DNP=void conditioning.

resolution.step: Acquire historical participation ground truth (free public snap-count/roster data), join to the player-events corpus, and re-evaluate every family under participation-true conditioning: absent+played -> 0, absent+did-not-play -> void. That re-receipt is a GOVERNED family-conditioning change: promotion states re-derive from it and publication follows the receipts, wherever they land.
resolution.interim: Published boards stay as receipted (their stated conditioning was applied consistently and the pessimistic bound does not prove failure — it proves sensitivity); this annex and the register record the caveat immediately.
